text:
sarah: saw p99 jump ~2.3x on prod between 03:10-03:30 UTC after the kernel-selection autotuner landed. p50/p95 mostly fine, tails exploded. attaching quick profiler snapshot.
mike: ouch. do we know which kernel variant? the autotuner flips between fast-f32 -> quant-int8 paths right?
sarah: yep. seems to coincide with a switch to the new "matmul_fast_v2" kernel on longer sequences. trace shows big memcpy stalls and extra kernel launches for sequences >1024.
raj: could be KV-cache eviction interplay. if KV hits drop, we refill and trigger different code paths. any cache-miss rate numbers?
sarah: cache hit % dropped from 98.6% -> 89.2% for that workload. suspect prefix cache fragmentation for multi-tenant requests. profiling snippet:
```
GPU timeline: kernel_launch( matmul_fast_v2 ) x 3
memcpy H2D spikes at 1.2ms
cpu wait on cuLaunch at 600us
KV lookup miss rate: 10.8%
queue depth: median 24 -> 42 during the spike
```
olivia: increased queue depth means our microbatcher kept packing despite slower kernel. headroom evaporated, so p99 spikes. what were target util numbers? we tuned to 92% busy earlier.
mike: 92% is aggressive for tail SLOs. we usually recommend 70-80% target for p99-sensitive endpoints. if autotuner optimizes for throughput it will push util up and hide tail risk.
dmitri: agree. options: 1) reduce target util / add headroom, 2) change admission control to cap queue depth per-GPU, 3) add a kernel fallback policy that picks the safer kernel for requests flagged as latency-sensitive.
raj: +1 for kernel fallback. we can detect high seq lengths or KV-miss-heavy prefixes and force the older matmul_stable kernel which has lower variance. cost will increase but p99 improves.
sarah: can we do dynamic fallback w/ a simple rule: if cache_hit < 95% OR seq_len > 1024 -> prefer stable kernel? cheap to implement in router.
mike: also consider per-model microbatch caps: seq_len-aware microbatcher that reduces batch size for long sequences. keeps tail low while maintaining throughput for short seqs.
olivia: two quick experiments: A) Canary: route 5% of traffic for that model to fallback kernel + seq-aware microbatching. B) Admission tweak: cap queue depth to 20 and measure p95/p99 and overall throughput.
dmitri: I'll wire a quick perf job and run it on canary cluster. perf-bot: please schedule a flamegraph run for the failing timeslice and store artifacts in s3://redwood-perf/1764805123/

perf-bot: scheduled job perf-1764805123, link https://perf.redwood.internal/1764805123 (results ETA 25m) :hourglass:
raj: also leaving a note: if we add fallback, ensure the kernel-selection telemetry logs which rule fired. we need to trace cost delta per request to justify fallback.
sarah: good point. add request tag and top-level metric: fallback_rate. we'll track p50/p95/p99 and token-cost. plan: run A/B for 24h, roll back if cost > +12% with no p99 improvement.
mike: sounds good. add a short-run that artificially reduces target util to 75% so we can compare headroom vs fallback impact.
dmitri: starting canary changes now. will post updates and the perf flamegraph link when ready.
olivia: thanks team. if we see similar regressions on other models, we should consider making the autotuner aware of tail-latency penalty (objective = latency_variance * alpha + throughput).
sarah: noted. will add a ticket to eng-runtime backlog: autotuner tail-awareness + seq-aware microbatch policies. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
